source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 12. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

learn.en: The tongue is small, but every word we say is written down. (Qur'an 50:18)
learn.title: Every word is written

learn.en: Lying is saying what is not true. Backbiting (ghībah) is talking about someone behind their back in a way they would not like — even if it is true.
learn.title: Lying and backbiting

learn.en: Slander is saying something bad about someone that is not true. Namīmah is carrying words between people to make them fight.
learn.title: Slander and tale-carrying

learn.en: “Truthfulness leads to goodness, and goodness leads to Paradise.” (Bukhari 6094)
learn.title: Truth leads to Paradise

learn.en: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or keep silent.” (Bukhari 6018)
learn.title: Good words or silence

learn.en: Before you speak, ask three questions: Is it true? Is it kind? Is it needed? If the talk turns to backbiting, change the subject or defend the person.
learn.title: Three questions

opts: Talking about someone in a way they would dislike, behind their back

quiz.en: True or false? A small lie for a joke is fine.
True or false? If what I say about someone is true, it can still be backbiting.
True or false? Passing on a rumour without checking is fine.

move.ar: ضَعْ إِصْبَعَكَ عَلَى فَمِكَ: قُلْ خَيْرًا أَوِ اصْمُتْ!
move.en: Finger on your lips: say something good — or stay quiet!

think.q: Your friends start making fun of a classmate who isn't there. What could you say?
think.a: Change the subject, or say something good about him — “Let's not talk about him when he's not here.”

parents.summary: Lying, backbiting, slander and tale-carrying harm us and others. Speak the truth, say good words, or stay silent. Ask: true? kind? needed?
parents.tip: Play “true, kind, needed?” at dinner with pretend sentences.
